Perfect! I've successfully added a due date field to the item creation form. Here's what I implemented:

## Summary of Changes

### Backend (backend/app/models.py)
- Added `due_date: datetime | None = Field(default=None)` to the **ItemBase** class
- Added `due_date: datetime | None = None` to the **ItemPublic** class for API responses

### Database Migration (backend/app/alembic/versions/001_add_due_date_to_item.py)
- Created a new Alembic migration that adds the `due_date` column to the `item` table
- The migration includes both upgrade and downgrade functions

### Frontend Types (frontend/src/client/types.gen.ts)
- Added `due_date?: (string | null)` to the **ItemCreate** type
- Added `due_date?: (string | null)` to the **ItemPublic** type

### Frontend Form (frontend/src/components/Items/AddItem.tsx)
- Added `due_date: z.string().optional().nullable()` to the Zod form schema
- Added `due_date: null` to the form's default values
- Added a new form field with a **datetime-local input** that provides a native browser date/time picker
- The form now includes three fields:
  - **Title** (required, marked with red asterisk)
  - **Description** (optional)
  - **Due Date** (optional)

### Key Features
✅ **All existing fields continue working** - title and description work exactly as before  
✅ **Due date is optional** - users can create items without selecting a date  
✅ **Native date picker** - uses HTML5 `datetime-local` input for better UX  
✅ **Form validation** - integrates with existing form validation  
✅ **Build succeeds** - no TypeScript or compilation errors

The form is ready to use. When the backend is running and the database migration is applied, users will be able to select a due date when creating items.
